design_principle: The overlay should tell a visual story, not decorate the video. Evidence, comparison and correction must be distinguishable.

render_rules: Never show more than one correction concept at a time in player mode.
Use slow motion only around the relevant phase, then return to a clean full-speed replay.
Ghost/reference overlays must represent a range or matched example—not a universal ideal skeleton.
Use text labels for confidence when a marker is estimated.
Show strengths in green/positive semantics in implementation, but do not encode color as the only signal for accessibility.
Corrections should use motion arrows/path corridors; static angle arcs are coach-mode unless essential.
In player mode, default to no skeleton. Render only the body/racket/ball evidence needed for the thesis.
Synchronize comparisons by tennis events (bounce/contact), not raw video start time.
Use a moving causal link to connect an upstream change to a downstream consequence.
Never display a crisp ghost/reference overlay when alignment or measurement uncertainty is poor.
Numbers should answer a player question; otherwise keep them in advanced/coach mode.
